q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: WITH CTE AS ( SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) AS CT FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID) SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CTE WHERE CT = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2_prompt_sql: WITH CTE AS ( SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) AS CT FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID) SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CTE WHERE CT = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2), (3); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 1), (2, 2);
explanation: Q1 groups all customers together and checks if the count of distinct products they purchased is equal to the total count of distinct products in the PRODUCT table. Q2, on the other hand, groups customers by their ID and checks if any of them purchased all distinct products. Q1 will return a result if all customers together have purchased all products, while Q2 will return a result if any single customer has purchased all products.
counterexample_dsp: Create a scenario where there are 3 products and 2 customers. Customer 1 has purchased all 3 products, and Customer 2 has purchased only 2 products. Q1 should return Customer 1, while Q2 should return Customer 1 as well.
